nodes.label: The electromagnetic index is a quotient, not an extension
nodes.rationale: Every electromagnetic quantity a transition carries (Delta-l, Delta-spin, multipole) is a function of coordinates Lambda already holds; a derived coordinate determines no new cell, so it adds no join-irreducible and cannot enlarge the closed family — it only enlarges the ambient box the family is measured against. Hence the electromagnetic content of Lambda is read off (a quotient by a symmetry, Noether), never added.

nodes.label: E = 3,900 for the electromagnetic adjunction to Lambda-9
nodes.rationale: Adjoining the electromagnetic coordinates as new axes grows the ambient box by each new coordinate's value count while the cell count does not move, so defect zero becomes defect 3,900 — a derived coordinate strictly worsens closure.

nodes.label: Lambda's image on (multipole, Delta-S) is the complete rectangle, E = 0
nodes.rationale: E = 0 for the empty reason that a full box always closes — measured on Lambda-9 at the caps of §7.4, (n,e,l,k,f) = (3,3,1,3,1).

nodes.label: Electromagnetic and composition predicates are near-independent at 0.0004 of 0.633 bits
nodes.rationale: The transit condition decides state succession, the electromagnetic condition decides radiation; they share almost no information on the same cells, so the index carries both without their being one question.

nodes.label: A selection rule is a quotient by a symmetry
nodes.rationale: Prior art is the symmetry-conservation correspondence (Noether 1918, Wigner 1927); Lambda was already carrying its quotient before the electromagnetic coordinates were named.
